status: Desktop-emulated regression verified; physical iPhone confirmation pending
trigger: User reported a repeated browser-page crash after several scrolls on a physical iPhone.
hypothesis: Large composited paper surfaces and separately promoted shading layers plausibly contributed to rendering pressure. The physical crash cause has not been proven.

measurement.engine: Playwright Chromium153, software compositing on the verification host
measurement.units: MiB of theoretical full-resolution RGBA surface area, not measured resident GPU memory

projectBudgets.qualification: Conservative project regression budgets; not universal Safari or iOS safety limits.

regression.test: tests/e2e/proposal.spec.ts: high-density mobile paper stays within its compositing budget through zooms and reversals
regression.baseline: Fails: six drawn paper faces exceed the project budget.
regression.candidate: All budget assertions passed; includes every mobile reading target and repeated reversals.
regression.recovery: Explicit ?view=read overrides a saved tour preference and preserves normal reading through notes navigation.

limitations: The desktop emulation did not reproduce the physical iPhone browser crash.
Layer dimensions and surface-area estimates do not measure actual allocation, tiling, cache residency or peak iOS memory.
Desktop RAF timing does not prove that every frame was painted or predict iPhone frame rate.
WebKit screenshot, IntersectionObserver, transparent-ancestor hit-testing and headful viewport limitations remain documented in webkit-verification.json.
